title: ART DECO STYLE BREAKFRONT DISP...
reason: Art Deco style curved-glass display cabinet; a sound 1930s to 1940s one makes about $100 to $250, but this is sold as is with veneer checking.
findings: Two photos (whole cabinet, and a close-up of the door and centre stile). Curved-glass display cabinet in a figured dark walnut-type veneer: flat glazed central door with a cream, ivory-like pull handle and a key hanging on a string tag, D-shaped curved glass ends, two curved glass shelves, what looks like a mirrored back panel (the room is reflected in it) and bun feet. The form is a typical 1930s to 1940s Australian Art Deco china cabinet, though the title says 'style' so it could be a later copy. No maker's label, retailer plate or stamp is visible; the only writing is lot ticket 338.
condition: Sold as is per the title. The veneer on the curved front stile shows fine horizontal splits (checking) and the finish is dry and dull. The glass door, curved side glass and shelves look intact in both photos and the key is present. Back, interior hardware and underside were not seen.
rescore_note: Curved-glass walnut-veneer display cabinet of the 1930s to 40s Australian Art Deco type with intact glass, shelves, key and bun feet, but no maker, 'style' may mean a later copy, and the finish is dry with veneer checking on the curved stile; a common type in tired condition, mid-low band.
